v1.feedback: Strong concept — Gonzalez-Torres light strings via differential growth with a faint spectral moonbow sweep is poetically apt and the palette (amber base, HSL-safe desaturated pastels for the moonbow wash) clears the saturation gate cleanly. The differential growth sim with spatial hashing is solid. Two refinements: the 40k particle scatter around a ~3200-vertex spine risks reading as a fuzzy halo rather than distinct incandescent bulbs — consider reducing particle count or tightening the scatter radius so individual 'bulbs' resolve as discrete warm points along the catenary. Second, the moonbow sweep phase could benefit from a slightly longer dwell at peak (currently it may flash past too quickly for dark-adapted perception) — stretch the visible window from ~3s to ~5s so the spectral wash registers as a contemplative event rather than a flicker.

v2.feedback: Strong concept marriage — Gonzalez-Torres catenary strings with a rare-event moonbow wash is poetic and the desaturated 6-stop spectral gradient stays firmly in restrained territory. Consider slowing the moonbow onset ramp beyond 25s so the viewer truly forgets it's coming; at 25s in a gallery tab it may feel periodic rather than rare. The 18k particle count with tight scatter risks reading as solid tubes rather than discrete bulb-on-wire; dropping to ~12k or adding per-bulb size variation via the seed attribute would recover the Gonzalez-Torres filament delicacy.
